thesis: The servant must know Allah through both expansive mercy and serious punishment, and the announcement deliberately opens with belonging ('My servants') and forgiveness before it moves to warning.
notes: Thesis is carried explicitly by Ibn Kathir on 15:49-50: 'Similar Ayat to this have already been quoted above, which indicate that we must always be in a state between hope (for Allah's mercy) and fear (of His punishment).' The file's Theme 2 (mercy stated first so despair does not disable tawbah) is independently carried by al-Tabari, who cites the hadith of Jibril: 'Ya Muhammad, inna Allaha yaqul: lima tuqannitu 'ibadi? Nabbi' 'ibadi anni ana al-Ghafur al-Rahim...' plus the Qatadah report on knowing the measure of Allah's pardon and of His punishment. Mechanically verified against scripts/.corpus-cache/quranic-corpus.json: nabbi' is the first word of 15:49 (the sequence opens with the rub' mark, not a word), root=نبأ pos=V; al-Ghafur (root غفر) precedes al-Rahim (root رحم) in the named pair; 'adhabi at 15:50:2 (root عذب) is the possessive form the file leans on; huwa at 15:50:3 is the separating pronoun. No countable/'only place'/hapax claims are made anywhere in the file. No tafsir is named or quoted in the file, so there is nothing to mis-attribute and no 500-char truncation artifact. No ahkam content. One optional refinement for the human, not a flag: al-Tabari, al-Muyassar and al-Jalalayn all restrict al-Ghafur al-Rahim to those who repent/believe (al-Muyassar: 'al-ghafur lil-mu'minin al-ta'ibin ... wa 'adhabi huwa al-'adhab al-mu'lim ... li-ghayr al-ta'ibin'), while the file states the two names unqualified in Part 1; the file recovers this in Theme 2 by tying mercy to actual tawbah, so nothing is misstated.

thesis: The deepest misguidance is not merely committing a wrong but inheriting it, sacralizing it, and attributing it to Allah, so that one walks with devils as allies while still feeling guided.

flags.quote: Worship is placed under the horizon of return. The One who originated you is the One before whom your religion will be measured.
flags.issue: The file states one side of an ikhtilaf that both fetched primary sources explicitly name as disputed. al-Tabari on 7:29: 'qala Abu Ja'far: ikhtalafa ahl al-ta'wil fi ta'wil qawlihi: kama bada'akum ta'udun' and then lays out two schools -- (a) you were begun shaqi/sa'id, mu'min/kafir, and you will be raised the same way (Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id b. Jubayr 'kama kutiba 'alaykum takunun', Muhammad b. Ka'b, al-Suddi), and (b) as He created you from nothing you will be returned after annihilation (al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd). Ibn Kathir likewise: 'There is some difference over the meaning of ... (As He brought you in the beginning, so shall you be brought into being again),' and notes Ibn Jarir preferred one and Ibn 'Abbas the other. The file's reading matches al-Tabari's and al-Jalalayn's preferred position, so it is not false -- but it is presented as the plain meaning with no signal that the alternative reading exists, and the alternative is the qadar-loaded one (born believer/disbeliever, raised as such, tied to 64:2).

flags.quote: This is a devastating ending. The tragedy is not only that they are astray. It is that they misperceive their condition. They are allied elsewhere while feeling secure in themselves.
flags.issue: This, plus 'Then the diagnostic cause:' at line 185 and 'The cure for self-deceived religion is not self-confidence. It is sincere reorientation before the Lord who began us and to whom we return' at line 211, is the file's entire treatment of 'fariqan hada wa fariqan haqqa 'alayhim al-dalalah'. It reads the division in a purely human-agency register: they chose devils as allies, therefore they went astray, therefore the remedy is sincere self-reorientation. The causal half is genuinely grounded -- al-Tabari: 'inna al-fariq alladhi haqqa 'alayhim al-dalalah innama dallu ... bi-ttikhadhihim al-shayatin nusara' min dun Allah' -- but the file drops the divine-decree half that all four fetched sources foreground, and gives no hint that the ayah is a contested proof-text. al-Tabari immediately before that: 'thumma ibtada'a al-khabar jalla thana'uhu 'amma sabaqa min 'ilmihi fi khalqihi, wa jara bihi fihim qada'uhu, fa-qala: hada Allahu minhum fariqan fa-waffaqahum ...'. al-Muyassar: 'ja'ala Allahu 'ibadahu fariqayn: fariqan waffaqahum lil-hidayah ... wa fariqan wajabat 'alayhim al-dalalah'. Ibn Kathir spends most of the comment on qadar (the Bukhari hadith of the Book that precedes the deed, 'He has decided that some of them will be miserable and some will be happy', 87:3, 20:50). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir then state outright that this ayah settles a live inter-school dispute -- al-Tabari: 'wa hadha min abyan al-dalalah 'ala khata' qawl man za'ama anna Allaha la yu'adhdhibu ahadan 'ala ma'siyah rakibaha aw dalalah i'taqadaha illa an ya'tiyaha ba'da 'ilm ...'. Under rubric check 4 a contested passage must acknowledge the ikhtilaf or mark the reading as one reading; this file does neither, and the omission systematically favors one theological side.

notes: Not a false thesis -- the hook (inherited fahishah + false attribution to Allah + self-satisfied misguidance) is directly carried by Ibn Kathir, al-Tabari (Mujahid/Ibn 'Abbas/al-Suddi on tawaf performed naked and defended as 'wajadna 'alayha aba'ana wa Allahu amarana biha'), al-Muyassar and al-Jalalayn. Verified mechanically against the corpus: in 7:28 the ancestry defense (wajadna 'alayha aba'ana) does precede the divine attribution (wa Allahu amarana biha), so the file's 'two-layer shield' ordering is correct; the morphology comment roots (فحش, قسط, خلص, فرق, ضلل, شطن, ولي, هدي, حسب) all match the segment list. qist=al-'adl is exactly Mujahid and al-Suddi in al-Tabari and al-Jalalayn. No countable, 'only place', hapax, or 'never/always' claims appear in the file, so nothing else needed corpus verification. No truncation artifacts (the file quotes no tafsir text). SPECIFIC FIX: (1) after 'Just as He began you, you will return', add one sentence flagging that the commentators divide here -- al-Tabari records both 'you are raised as you were begun, believer and disbeliever' (Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid) and 'you are returned after annihilation as you were created from nothing' (al-Hasan, Qatadah), and prefers the second; (2) in section 5 and Theme 2, add the decree side before the human-agency reading -- e.g. that al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir read 'fariqan hada' as Allah's prior knowledge and decree running upon His creation (with tawfiq as the guided group's cause), while 'innahum ittakhadhu al-shayatin awliya'' supplies the human ground of the second group's dalalah; and mark explicitly that this ayah sits inside the classical qadar dispute rather than resolving it in the reader's ear. A third, lesser gap worth a line while the human is in the file: al-Tabari also records ikhtilaf on 'aqimu wujuhakum 'inda kulli masjid' (face the Ka'bah wherever you pray -- Mujahid, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd -- vs. make your prostration purely for Allah -- al-Rabi', which Abu Ja'far prefers); the file's gloss follows the preferred reading but again presents it as the only one.

thesis: False worship is not dignified by age, disagreement over revelation is an old human pattern rather than a verdict on this Prophet, and the delay of judgment ends in full undiminished repayment.
notes: All three limbs of the thesis are carried by the fetched sources. Inherited worship without proof: al-Tabari on 11:109 -- 'lam ya'budu ma 'abadu min al-awthan illa ittiba'an minhum minhaj aba'ihim ... la 'an amr Allah iyyahum bi-dhalik, wa la bi-hujjah tabayyanuha tujibu 'alayhim 'ibadataha'; Ibn Kathir: 'they have no support for their Shirk. They are only mimicking their fathers in ignorance.' Musa's Book as consolation: al-Tabari opens 11:110 with 'musalliyan nabiyyahu fi takdhib mushriki qawmihi ... bi-fi'l Bani Isra'il bi-Musa', matching the file's 'the Prophet is not being singled out for rejection'. Deferred judgment by a prior word: al-Tabari 'lawla kalimah sabaqat ... bi-annahu la yu'ajjilu 'ala khalqihi al-'adhab, walakin yata'anna hatta yablugha al-kitabu ajalah'; al-Jalalayn 'bi-ta'khir al-hisab wal-jaza' lil-khala'iq ila yawm al-qiyamah'; Ibn Kathir quoting Ibn Jarir plus 17:15 and 20:129-130. The one structural claim is verified mechanically: the w-f-y frame is real -- scripts/.corpus-cache/quranic-corpus.json has 11:109:17:2 مُوَفُّو (ACT_PCPL, VF:2, ROOT:وفي) and 11:111:4:2 يُوَفِّيَ (IMPF, VF:2, ROOT:وفي), i.e. the same root in the same Form II, opening-and-closing the section exactly as the file says. The file's only explicit tafsir attribution -- 'whether worldly allotment, deferred punishment, or final recompense as the tafsir explains' -- matches: al-Tabari transmits Ibn 'Abbas 'ma wu'idu fihi min khayr aw sharr' / 'ma quddira lahum min al-khayr wal-sharr' and Ibn Zayd 'nasibuhum min al-'adhab'; al-Jalalayn 'hazzuhum min al-'adhab'; Ibn Kathir adds worldly reward for any good deeds. No countable, superlative-count, hapax or 'only place' claims anywhere in the file. No ahkam-bearing or contested material -- 11:110's 'kalimah sabaqat' is handled as delay of judgment, which is the tafsirs' own reading, and the file does not push it into a qadar claim. No quoted tafsir, so no 500-char truncation artifact. Two soft, non-blocking observations for the human: the gloss 'miryah is not just a light question. It carries the feel of unsettled, troubling doubt' is a lexical shade the file supplies itself (al-Tabari and al-Muyassar both gloss miryah simply as shakk) -- defensible from the root م-ر-ي but unattributed; and Ibn Kathir notes 'many different modes of recitation' for 11:111 (the lamma/lamma qira'at), which the file neither uses nor misstates.
